answer: Reputation-weighted message routing, or the raven rule: an identity's influence scales with accurately predicted peer behavior, and each new identity starts at the network's minimum weight. A cipher handshake proves control of a key, but trust only accrues through fulfilled predictions, so cloning yields many powerless voices rather than one loud one. An attacker must run real, costly interactions for every clone—paying saffron-priced bandwidth and compute per identity—while honest agents pay nothing extra for their single identity.
